materialPlan.woodRule: Wood needs believable board direction, grain scale, end grain, joinery, sealing, wear, and moisture response appropriate to indoor, residential, marine, fantasy, or industrial use.
materialPlan.flexibleRule: Fabric, upholstery, leather, rubber, and flexible polymers require thickness, seams, compression or tension cues, stitching where visible, and roughness variation tied to handling.
materialPlan.emissiveRule: Emissive accents must arise from a lens, strip, screen, projector, fixture, biological organ, or energy component. Do not paint unexplained neon lines across ordinary structure.

townArtDirection.style: luxury hillside realism; stone, stucco, glass, landscaped masonry, premium vehicles, gated civic and residential architecture

productionBrief.conditionAndWear: Keep premium public surfaces clean and maintained. Wear remains subtle at tires, drainage paths, handles, outdoor contact points, service access, staff-only areas, and concealed back-of-house zones.

interactionAndAnimation.guidance: Keep access panels, doors, lights, propulsion units, controls, cargo areas, steering surfaces, lift hardware, and service interfaces separately named for animation, customization, damage, maintenance, and gameplay states.
hooks: changeable display, content, or emissive state
day, night, powered, warning, and damaged light states
moving propulsion, steering, mechanism, or operating component
seating, occupancy, or interaction sockets
pickup, open, consume, empty, stack, carry, or discard state

productionBrief.collision: Use a stable chassis or hull collider with optional cabin, cargo, propulsion, or hit-region hulls. Do not trace every light, mirror, vent, wheel, pod, railing, rope, or fastener. Entry sockets and clearance volumes must align with the visible body.
productionBrief.orientationAndPivot: Use positive Z as forward and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at the ground, waterline, rail, or hover-plane center below the chassis or hull, with separate transforms for propulsion and steering hardware.
productionBrief.optimization: Use sufficient geometry for reflective silhouette surfaces while economizing hidden undersides. Reuse repeated seats, lights, vents, wheels, pods, rails, and fasteners. LODs must preserve occupancy and propulsion logic.

lod.lod0: Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 39,000 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it.
lod.lod1: Medium-range output should target roughly 18,000 triangles while preserving primary form, supports, interaction components, openings, material blocks, and essential lights.
lod.lod2: Far output should target roughly 6,000 triangles or a suitable impostor while retaining the recognizable outline, mounting or ground relationship, and major color or emissive signature.
lod.neverCollapse: The transportation class must read from front, side, rear, and three-quarter views through stance, cabin or operator placement, overhangs, propulsion spacing, body volumes, glazing, and travel direction before decals or glow are considered.

Material boundaries follow real construction, growth, preparation, packaging, or manufacturing and do not act as arbitrary color blocking.
Transparent, flexible, organic, masonry, food, metal, wood, liquid, and emissive materials use believable thickness and response where present.

humans assembled from cylinders and spheres without credible anatomy, clothing, hands, feet, face structure, and rigging
monsters or animals represented by stacked circles, repeated blobs, or disconnected primitive piles

hover vehicles that are only a floating box or toy saucer
buildings that are only an undecorated rectangular shell when the specification requires a functional facade
one-material assets when the real object clearly contains distinct materials

random neon on assets whose town profile does not call for neon
